title: Lester plays Singing the Blues; learning In A Mist in three-part harmony
summary: Lester played Singing the Blues around the house; Phillips explains records seldom named players, and how Lester gave Phillips and Pete Jones harmony parts for Bix's In A Mist.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: [END OF TAPE 1, SIDE 2]
When the tape went off, you were mentioning "Singing The Blues" and what you all did with that record, and what you did with other records. Could you repeat that, please?
"Singing the Blues," when we heard it, he was playing it -- he was playing around in the house.
Who was that?
Les. Les was playing "Singing The Blues," you know.
Now, this is "Singing The Blues" by Frankie Trumbauer and his Orchestra, with Bix Beiderbecke.
Phillips - 59

Yeah, Frankie... Yeah, there was about five or six of them. And I was listening to it, I said, "Man, who's that cat blowin' that trumpet?" -- like that, you know. He said, "His name is Bix." At that time, you had to know who it was, because they didn't put the names on the records. Very few records that they had on there who was playing, like individual players, you know. They didn't have it on there too much. You know what I mean? You just had to know who was... Sometimes they did. Maybe one, like Louis, his name was on there with Bessie Smith when she sang the "St. Louis Blues," that he's playing behind, and different tunes he was playing behind her. But they just had the band on there, like Red Nichols and His Five Pennies... See, Bix made some records, too, under his name. "In A Mist." We used to play that, too. That's Bix's tune. He wrote that, "In A Mist."
Lester used to listen to that?
Yeah.
That piano piece.
Piano piece.
What did Lester think about that? I know that it had some kind of interesting harmonies in it, some interesting chords.
Fine. We all did, you know. See, we learned that, to play it together.
You learned "In A Mist"?
Phillips - 60
Yeah.
Well, now me about that. What instrumentation did you use on that, and how did you pick up...?
We picked up the lead on it. Played the lead, and then... He played the lead on it, and then he gave us the harmony to it, and then after that...
Lester gave you the harmony?
Yeah. He was like that. He had that kind of ear.
He just did it naturally.

Yeah, naturally. He'd tell you, say, "I don't know what note it is for you. You hit this note, and you'll get a sound." So he couldn't tell you... At that time, he didn't know that. He wasn't familiar with chord progressions. But he said, "You play this note, Phil; Pete, you play this note." And he'd give it to us. "Now let's hit it together." It would come together like that. Pretty, three-part harmony.
And he did that on "In A Mist."
Yeah! But we didn't ad-lib it; we played it... It had a beat to it. Most all those tunes we played by Bix and Frankie and Red Nichols and all those tunes...
